title: Types of Capacitors Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's ceiling fan hums but will not start until it gets a push. The electrician swaps one small box marked 2.5 µF, 440 V. What do those numbers mean? In this animated lesson we sort capacitors into their two families: fixed capacitors named after their dielectric (ceramic, mica, paper or plastic film, electrolytic) and variable capacitors (the gang capacitor and the trimmer).

On a live breadboard we turn the knob of a gang capacitor in a radio's tuned circuit: the plate overlap grows, the capacitance climbs from 50 to 400 pF and the oscilloscope shows the tuned wave slowing from about 1400 kHz to 500 kHz. Then the three ratings on every capacitor: capacitance with tolerance, working voltage (and what happens above it) and polarity for electrolytic capacitors. We decode the three digit code with a worked example (473J = 47 nF ± 5%), then the exam trap (104 is not 104 pF), where it is asked, an original PUC board pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 28 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
